title: Outlook for iOS and Android: Purview label inheritance from email attachments
summary: The licensing guidance omits Microsoft's requirement to assign the standard/Plan 1 entitlement alongside a premium/P2 entitlement. The roadmap facts, portal paths and PowerShell calls are supported; the briefing correctly reports the disagreement over mobile availability.

claims.claim: The roadmap feature is sensitivity label inheritance from attachments in Outlook for iOS and Android.
claims.quote: Outlook for iOS and Android will support Microsoft Purview sensitivity label inheritance from attachments.

claims.claim: Outlook can automatically apply an email sensitivity label when users attach sensitivity-labelled files.
claims.quote: When users attach files with sensitivity labels, Outlook can automatically apply or recommend an email sensitivity label based on organizational policy settings.

claims.claim: Outlook can recommend an email sensitivity label based on its attachments.
claims.quote: When users attach files with sensitivity labels, Outlook can automatically apply or recommend an email sensitivity label based on organizational policy settings.

claims.claim: The mobile inheritance behaviour follows organisational policy settings.
claims.quote: Outlook can automatically apply or recommend an email sensitivity label based on organizational policy settings.

claims.claim: The roadmap says inheritance reduces manual labelling effort.
claims.quote: This helps organizations maintain consistent data classification and protection while reducing manual labeling effort.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters; rationale: risk; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Inheritance requires an administrator to enable it in a sensitivity label policy.
claims.quote: You configure this setting in the sensitivity label policy, on the Default settings for emails page. For the section Inherit label from attachments, select the checkbox Email inherits highest priority label from attachments.

claims.claim: Policy-based sensitivity labelling is included in the named Microsoft 365 E5 entitlement rather than separately metered for this option.
claims.quote: Sensitivity labeling, including automatic or policy-based labeling, requires a Microsoft 365 E5 license or Microsoft 365 Information Protection and Governance (IPG).

claims.where: Cost and licensing; front matter: licensing.notes; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The licensing requirement is Microsoft 365 E5 or Microsoft 365 Information Protection and Governance, without stating the additional standard/Plan 1 assignment requirement for premium/P2 users.
claims.quote: A standard/Plan 1 license must be assigned in addition to the premium/P2 license for users to have access to sensitivity labeling for Information Protection for Office 365 and AIP, even if the premium licenses/Plan 2 are assigned.
claims.fix: Keep the E5/IPG requirement and add to the licensing notes and Cost and licensing: 'For users assigned a premium/P2 entitlement, the standard/Plan 1 entitlement must also be assigned for sensitivity labeling to be available.' Cite the existing Microsoft Purview service description.

claims.claim: The service description has no separate feature row for attachment label inheritance.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Outlook label inheritance email attachments licensing price meter minimum mobile version'; read the Purview service description's sensitivity-labeling section and its complete feature tables. No attachment-inheritance row is present.

claims.claim: Sensitivity labels in Office apps require a subscription edition of Office.
claims.quote: To use sensitivity labels in Office apps, you must use a subscription edition of Office.

claims.claim: No meter is documented specifically for attachment inheritance as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Outlook label inheritance email attachments licensing price meter minimum mobile version'; opened the Office-apps inheritance documentation and the Purview service description, including all sensitivity-labeling tables. Neither documents an attachment-inheritance meter.

claims.claim: The printed Microsoft Purview portal path reaches the attachment-inheritance checkbox in an existing publishing policy.
claims.quote: Default settings for emails ... Inherit label from attachments ... Email inherits highest priority label from attachments. [create-sensitivity-labels:] Solutions > Information Protection > Publishing policies. ... select it, and then select the Edit Policy button

claims.claim: Set-LabelPolicy -Identity Global -AdvancedSettings @{AttachmentAction="Automatic"} enables automatic attachment-label inheritance.
claims.quote: AttachmentAction: Unlabeled emails inherit the highest priority label from file attachments. Set the value to Automatic (to automatically apply the label) ... Example: Set-LabelPolicy -Identity Global -AdvancedSettings @{AttachmentAction="Automatic"}.

claims.claim: The printed Microsoft Purview portal path reaches the recommendation option under attachment inheritance in an existing publishing policy.
claims.quote: Recommend users apply the attachments label instead of automatically applying it. [create-sensitivity-labels:] Solutions > Information Protection > Publishing policies. ... select it, and then select the Edit Policy button

claims.claim: Set-LabelPolicy -Identity Global -AdvancedSettings @{AttachmentAction="Recommended"} selects recommendation rather than automatic application.
claims.quote: AttachmentAction: Unlabeled emails inherit the highest priority label from file attachments. Set the value to Automatic (to automatically apply the label) or Recommended (as a recommended prompt to the user.

claims.claim: The policy settings apply to the users and groups to whom that sensitivity label policy is published.
claims.quote: As part of the label policy, you select users and groups to have sensitivity labels and label policy settings.

claims.claim: Set-LabelPolicy works only in Security & Compliance PowerShell.
claims.quote: This cmdlet is functional only in Security & Compliance PowerShell.

claims.claim: The recommendation option is available after selecting the inheritance checkbox.
claims.quote: When you select this checkbox, you can then further select the following option: Recommend users apply the attachments label instead of automatically applying it.

claims.claim: With inheritance enabled, the label is applied automatically unless the recommendation option is selected.
claims.quote: Without this selection, the label is automatically applied but users can still remove the label or select a different label before sending the email.

claims.claim: Users can remove an automatically inherited label before sending, subject to other policy settings.
claims.quote: Without this selection, the label is automatically applied but users can still remove the label or select a different label before sending the email.

claims.claim: Users can select a different label before sending an email with an automatically inherited label.
claims.quote: users can still remove the label or select a different label before sending the email.

claims.claim: Inheritance selects a label for an email that has not been manually labelled.
claims.quote: Turn on email inheritance for when users attach labeled documents to an email message that isn't manually labeled.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Inheritance selects from attachment labels published to the user.
claims.quote: a sensitivity label is dynamically selected for the email message, based on the sensitivity labels that are applied to the attachments and published to the user.

claims.claim: Outlook selects the highest priority eligible attachment label when it supports inheritance.
claims.quote: The highest priority label is dynamically selected when it's supported by Outlook.

claims.claim: Attachment inheritance does not replace a manually applied email label.
claims.quote: When an email message has been manually labeled, that label won't be replaced by label inheritance from email attachments.

claims.claim: Inheritance replaces a lower priority automatically applied sensitivity label.
claims.quote: Label inheritance from email attachments will replace a lower priority sensitivity label that is automatically applied or applied as a default label, but won't override a higher priority label.

claims.claim: Inheritance replaces a lower priority default sensitivity label.
claims.quote: Label inheritance from email attachments will replace a lower priority sensitivity label that is automatically applied or applied as a default label, but won't override a higher priority label.

claims.claim: Inheritance does not override a higher priority email label.
claims.quote: Label inheritance from email attachments will replace a lower priority sensitivity label that is automatically applied or applied as a default label, but won't override a higher priority label.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Attachment inheritance requires a physical file attachment.
claims.quote: The attachment must be a physical file, and can't be a link to a file (for example, a link to a file on Microsoft SharePoint or OneDrive).

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Links to labelled files in SharePoint or OneDrive do not trigger attachment inheritance.
claims.quote: The attachment must be a physical file, and can't be a link to a file (for example, a link to a file on Microsoft SharePoint or OneDrive).

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance
claims.claim: By default, encryption from the automatically selected label is also applied to the email.
claims.quote: By default, if the automatically selected label applies encryption, the same encryption is applied to the email.

claims.claim: Learn describes DKE configurations in which no label or protection is selected for the email.
claims.quote: When Outlook doesn't support DKE: If the highest priority label applies Double Key Encryption, no label or encryption is selected for the email message in Outlook for Windows.

claims.claim: A highest priority attachment label configured only for user-defined Word, PowerPoint and Excel permissions does not select a label or protection for the email.
claims.quote: no label or protection is selected for the email message because Outlook doesn't support this label configuration.

claims.claim: Sensitivity labels in Outlook for iOS and Android require an Exchange Online mailbox.
claims.quote: For Outlook for Windows, Outlook for iOS and Android, Outlook on the web, and new Outlook for Windows, the mailbox must be hosted in Exchange Online.

claims.claim: Sensitivity labels in mobile Outlook are not supported for on-premises mailboxes.
claims.quote: Sensitivity labels aren't supported for mailboxes that are hosted on-premises.

claims.quote: Searched: 'Outlook label inheritance email attachments licensing price meter minimum mobile version'; read the complete inheritance row in sensitivity-labels-versions and inheritance section in sensitivity-labels-office-apps. Mobile entries say Not available, not a version.
